html:
The Barunggam are an Aboriginal Australian people of inland southeast Queensland, west of the Bunya Mountains. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them in detail. The Bunya Mountains nearby held great gatherings in the seasons when the bunya pine dropped its huge nutty cones, and peoples came from across the region to feast, trade and settle disputes. Neighbours on the map include the Mandandanji, the Wuli Wuli and the Bigambul. Squatters took up land on the Darling Downs from 1840. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
